summary: Greenlee County Forest Service tower built 1933 as an Aermotor MC-24 (31 ft 6 in); NHLR-registered 2009; still listed as standing and reached by trail.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-24 lookout (1933), tower about 31 ft 6 in

access.note: Reached by a Forest Service trail in the Blue Range Primitive Area (hikers and horseback riders; no motor or mechanized travel); no source says the tower itself is open to climbing

visit.trail_note: Trail is open to hiking and horseback riding; motorized and mechanized travel is prohibited

events.note: Aermotor MC-24 lookout with a 31-foot 6-inch tower; the register gives the same build year
Trail guide dates a bank robbery in McNary to 1921; the man was shot as he stepped out of the cabin
July 21, 1922 newsletter item: a bank robber was pursued to the lookout and shot at the guard cabin some weeks earlier
Cab remodeled with replaced windows and siding; source gives the 1960s only, so 1960 is a placeholder year
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on September 2, 2009
Wallow Fire of June 2011 severely affected the northwest part of the Blue Range Primitive Area; no source says the lookout was damaged

evidence.supports: built 1933 and sister structure to Big Lake Lookout
evidence.quote: Blue Lookout is a sister structure to Big Lake Lookout and was also built in 1933.

evidence.supports: reached by trail on the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forest

resolved_conflicts.field: date of the bank robber shooting
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The July 1922 newsletter says the shooting came some weeks before July 21, 1922; the trail guide dates the McNary bank robbery to 1921. The record reports both and does not pick one date.

corrections.why: Forest Lookouts gives a 31-foot 6-inch tower, about 9.6 m; no page read gives 9.4 m

sources.title: Blue Lookout Trail - # 71
sources.publisher: U.S. Forest Service, Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests

notes_for_editor: Brief height 9.4 m is not supported by any page read; 31 ft 6 in (about 9.6 m) is. No staffing or rental source was found, so no staffing key is set. Access 'public' covers trail access only; climbing status is unknown. The trail page titles it #71 but its trail log says #321; the story uses neither number. Used two web searches and about six page reads.
